content_voiceover: This slide lays out the blood bank workflow for patients on daratumumab, broken into three phases: before, during, and after treatment. Before starting the drug, get a baseline direct and indirect Coombs test, an antibody screen, and minor antigen typing for Rh, Kidd, Duffy, MNS, and Ss systems. During treatment, transfuse antigen-matched red cells and use either manual polybrene antibody testing or DTT treatment for the crossmatch. After treatment, continue transfusing antigen-matched red cells, and for up to six months after the last dose, you still need to use the manual polybrene method for antibody testing, because the drug can linger in circulation that long. One local practice point here, in this institution, manual polybrene testing and matching replaces the DTT treatment workflow that's more common in Western protocols. And the asterisk note emphasizes why minor antigen matching matters, you pre-type the patient's minor blood group antigens so you can transfuse antigen-compatible units and avoid provoking new alloantibody formation.
keypoints: Workflow has three phases: before, during, and after daratumumab therapy
Baseline Coombs test, antibody screen, and minor typing before starting the drug
During and after treatment, transfuse antigen-matched red cells
Manual polybrene testing needed for up to six months after the last dose
